source_name: Government of Montenegro (gov.me) — public consultation on Draft Law amending the Law on Payment Transactions
why_relevant: The primary-law layer under everything in this cell. CBCG drafted the amendments; the Ministry of Finance ran a 25-day public consultation (announced 15 April – 8 May 2026) that carries the legal basis for SEPA accession, instant-payment obligations and the National Payment Board. Consultation notices give the earliest sight of forthcoming participant mandates.

source_name: Poslovnik Vlade Crne Gore i Poslovnik Skupštine Crne Gore (procedural rulebooks)
why_relevant: Not news, but the schema for everything else: these rulebooks define the mandatory stages (nacrt -> javna rasprava -> izjava/tabela usklađenosti -> utvrđivanje na Vladi -> prvo/drugo čitanje -> amandmani -> usvajanje -> objavljivanje), the minimum consultation durations and the documents that must accompany each bill. Encoding them lets the pipeline predict what artefact should exist next and detect when one is missing.

source_name: Government of Montenegro (gov.me) — official Montenegrin-language reporting on MONEYVAL/IMF outcomes
why_relevant: The Montenegrin authorities' own local-language read-out of external assessments is the fastest indicator of which assessor recommendations the government intends to act on and by when. It names the specific legal instruments amended (Zakon o sprječavanju pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma, pravilnici) and the plenary dates — a bridge between the assessor cell and domestic implementation.

source_name: Javna rasprava reports on the Draft Consumer Protection Law (wapi.gov.me document endpoint)
why_relevant: Post-consultation reports list every comment received and the ministry's acceptance/rejection — a direct read on how consumer-protection obligations over financial services were shaped. Demonstrates that gov.me serves its PDFs from the wapi.gov.me endpoint, which is the pattern to target when harvesting Montenegrin government documents generally.

source_name: Montenegro 2025 Report (SWD(2025) 754 final) — full PDF
why_relevant: The single densest document of forward-looking regulatory obligations for Montenegrin banking and payments: per-chapter alignment verdicts, named directives/regulations still to be transposed, and next-year recommendations.

source_name: Zakon o objavljivanju propisa i drugih akata (publication law)
why_relevant: Defines what must be published in Službeni list Crne Gore, in what form, and the vacatio legis rule that fixes entry into force. Reference text for correctly computing 'stupa na snagu osmog dana od dana objavljivanja' and for asserting a legal publication obligation on any act the collector expects but cannot find.

source_name: UBCG — Statut, Program rada and Pregled rada (annual work programme / activity report)
why_relevant: The annual work programme and activity review state, in the association's own words, which draft laws and regulatory files it intends to engage on in the coming year and which it responded to in the previous one — an early-warning calendar for regulatory workstreams and consultation deadlines.

source_name: European Payments Council — SEPA geographical scope and scheme participation for Montenegro
why_relevant: The EPC is the gatekeeper of SEPA scheme adherence — its scope decisions, adherence register and scheme rulebook release calendar impose dated compliance obligations on Montenegrin banks independent of national law.

source_name: EU Delegation to Montenegro / EEAS — Montenegro operationally part of SEPA
why_relevant: EU-side confirmation of operational SEPA status and of the accession conditionality attached to payments alignment. Useful as an independent, dated corroboration layer for milestone claims and as a pointer to EU acquis chapters driving future payment mandates.

source_name: Erste Bank AD Podgorica – Halcom to eMon OfficeBanking migration notice
why_relevant: Bank-side customer-communication pages are an under-used disclosure channel: they name the outgoing and incoming vendor platform explicitly. This one documents a concrete supplier switch inside a private Montenegrin bank.

source_name: Program pristupanja Crne Gore Evropskoj uniji (PPCG) — accession programme, Chapter 4 & 9
why_relevant: The national EU-accession programme sets, per negotiating chapter, the specific laws and bylaws Montenegro commits to adopt and the quarter by which. Chapter 9 (financial services: payment services, capital movement, AML/CFT) and Chapter 4 name the Ministry of Finance, CBCG, Komisija za tržište kapitala and the insurance supervisor as responsible institutions. It is the multi-year deadline backbone behind individual bills.

source_name: Nacionalni odbor za platni promet (National Payment Board / Committee) — coverage and CBCG-hosted material
why_relevant: The coordination body that convenes CBCG, Ministry of Finance and the commercial banks on SEPA implementation results and payment-infrastructure milestones. Its formation depended on parliament passing the law; its meeting outcomes are where participant readiness and next deadlines get set. No standalone portal was found — currently reachable only via CBCG press items and national broadcaster reporting.

source_name: MINA / CdM economy desks — association statement wire (proxy for UBCG and UPCG positions)
why_relevant: National agency and portal coverage frequently carries the full text of association saopštenja that never appear on the associations' own sites — e.g. the 2026 UBCG assembly adopting a new Statute and a 2026-2031 financial framework, and its broadened remit into digitalisation/AI, ESG, AML/CFT and financial inclusion. Practical fallback channel for detecting association activity.

entity_name: ASEE / Asseco South Eastern Europe corporate site
source_name: ASEE / Asseco SEE — ChipCard regional card processor and Montenegrin bank card/POS deployments
why_relevant: Vendor-side visibility into who actually runs card issuing/acquiring processing and POS estates for Montenegrin banks. ChipCard (ASEE-owned) acts as a regional processor serving Montenegrin bank acquiring (ATM, POS, e-commerce); ASEE also supplied POS platform migrations to NLB Montenegro. Vendor press releases reveal switch/processing arrangements that no regulator publishes.

source_name: CEE Legal Matters — Comparative Legal Guide: Banking & Finance (Montenegro chapter)
why_relevant: Law-firm-authored comparative guide that states Montenegrin qualifying-holding thresholds and CBCG procedural deadlines (e.g. 60 working days to decide on a qualifying holding, extendable by 20/30) side-by-side with regional peers. Useful for encoding procedural deadline rules and for spotting divergence from Serbian/Croatian practice.

source_name: Chambers and Partners — Merger Control Global Practice Guide, Montenegro
why_relevant: Describes the competition-clearance leg of cross-border bank deals affecting Montenegro (thresholds, filing deadlines, the Agency for Protection of Competition), the second regulatory gate alongside CBCG qualifying-holding approval. Regional group consolidation triggers filings here first.

source_name: European Banking Authority (EBA) — cooperation with South-Eastern European supervisors
why_relevant: The EBA Memorandum of Cooperation, signed under the Vienna Initiative, formally binds Montenegro's CBCG into EU supervisory-college practice with BiH, RS, North Macedonia, Serbia and Albania. EBA guidelines and Q&As adopted at EU level are the template CBCG follows, usually with a lag — a strong forward indicator of Montenegrin rulemaking.

source_name: Hrvatska narodna banka (HNB) — twinning with Montenegro communications
why_relevant: Junior consortium partner publishing conference agendas and outputs of the 'Support for regulation of the financial services in Montenegro' twinning — an unusually specific window into which directives are being drafted into Montenegrin law.

source_name: NATLEX (ILO) — Montenegro legislation records with archived Službeni list PDFs
why_relevant: International body that mirrors Montenegrin Official Gazette texts as durable PDFs — a fallback copy when sluzbenilist.me paywalls or reorganises an issue.

source_name: IMF/World Bank FSAP — Montenegro Financial Sector Assessment Program technical notes
why_relevant: FSAP technical notes (banking supervision, stress testing, crisis management/resolution, AML) generate multi-year recommendation lists that Montenegrin authorities then implement; subsequent Article IVs explicitly track FSAP-recommendation implementation, making the FSAP the anchor document for a dated reform backlog.

source_name: Portal Analitika – IT sector / outsourcing regulation coverage
why_relevant: Covers the Montenegrin regulation of bank outsourcing/externalisation — the legal frame governing how banks select, contract and monitor IT suppliers. Bridges the A3 regulatory topic to the vendor-ecosystem cell and points to which supplier arrangements banks must document.

source_name: UNDP Montenegro — regulatory framework assessment for FinTech development (and similar donor diagnostics)
why_relevant: Donor-commissioned gap analyses map Montenegrin payments/fintech law against PSD2, EMD2 and e-IDAS and list what remains untransposed — an indirect but explicit inventory of alignment gaps.

source_name: Alta Pay Group d.o.o. Podgorica (Alta Pay Crna Gora)
why_relevant: Serbian Alta group's Montenegrin PI arm; group communications explicitly describe the ME expansion, that Alta Pay Podgorica and Montenegro Transfers Podgorica sit in the same group, and that Montenegro Transfers is the sole Western Union agent. Group-level PR is where licence and product news for this operator actually appears.

source_name: ECB — MIP News: roll-out of instant payment settlement service in the Western Balkans (TIPS-based)
why_relevant: Documents the multilateral agreement under which Banca d'Italia supplies a TIPS-based instant payment platform to Western Balkan central banks (Albania, BiH, Kosovo, Montenegro), with the platform targeted to operate by mid-2026 and multi-currency settlement. Explains why Montenegro's system is a 'TIPS Clone' and where future cross-border interlinking announcements will surface.

entity_name: ecoi.net mirror of EC Montenegro country reports
source_name: ecoi.net mirror of EC Montenegro country reports
why_relevant: Stable third-party archive of EC country reports; useful fallback when EC document-download URLs rotate (they are GUID-based and change per edition).

source_name: NVO / civil-society legislative-transparency watchdogs (Akcija za socijalnu pravdu, Institut alternativa, ODIHR opinions)
why_relevant: Reveals indirectly: these actors document where the law-making pipeline fails to publish what it must — notably campaigning for tabele usklađenosti to be published, and ODIHR's opinion on the Montenegrin legislative process (use of urgent procedure, skipped consultations). Essential for calibrating how much of the pipeline is actually observable and for spotting bills pushed through by skraćeni/hitni postupak.

source_name: The Fintech Times — Montenegro's Fintech Ecosystem in 2026
why_relevant: One of very few English-language ecosystem overviews of ME fintech; useful for cross-checking actor names and for the international framing of ME payments, but secondary and unverified in this pass.
